specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** is-this-a-normal-dip
**Library:** Chart.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of three pilot performance series shows a normal implementation dip, an unusually deep or late dip, or no dip, applying the stated rule, and correctly judging all three. **Prerequisites:** implementation dip, managing expectations, the rule for a normal dip (all defined in the section "Fullan, the Implementation Dip, and CBAM" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of 3 monthly series, the learner commits a judgment and also the month of the lowest point, before the sim reveals the correct answers. A judgment is correct when it matches the "Correct judgment" column in Content. Mastery is 3 of 3 judgments correct. Viewing a chart afterward is exploration. **Misconceptions:** (1) Any drop below baseline means the pilot is failing. (2) No drop means the pilot is going well. (3) A dip that lasts a year is normal. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging a series against explicit thresholds requires reading three numbers from the data: the depth, the time of the low point, and the time of recovery. The no-dip series tests whether the learner understands that a missing dip can signal shallow change. **Content:** The rule shown: A normal dip has its lowest point in months 2 to 4, is no deeper than 15 percent of the baseline, and is back at or above the baseline by month 8. A dip that is deeper than 15 percent, that bottoms after month 4, or that has not recovered by month 8 is "Deep or late: investigate." A series that never falls below 97 percent of the baseline is "No dip: check whether practice really changed." Baseline for all three series: 70 (percent correct at month 0). Three series, by month 0 to 12: | Month | Series A | Series B | Series C | |---|---|---|---| | 0 | 70 | 70 | 70 | | 1 | 68 | 69 | 70 | | 2 | 64 | 63 | 70 | | 3 | 63 | 58 | 71 | | 4 | 65 | 55 | 70 | | 5 | 68 | 54 | 71 | | 6 | 71 | 56 | 70 | | 7 | 73 | 58 | 71 | | 8 | 75 | 60 | 70 | | 9 | 76 | 62 | 71 | | 10 | 77 | 63 | 70 | | 11 | 78 | 64 | 71 | | 12 | 78 | 65 | 71 | Answers: | Series | Lowest point (month, value) | Depth as share of baseline | Recovery to baseline | Correct judgment | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | A | month 3, 63 | 10.0% | month 6 | Normal dip | The low is in months 2 to 4, the depth is under 15 percent, and recovery comes before month 8. | | B | month 5, 54 | 22.9% | not by month 12 | Deep or late: investigate | The low comes after month 4, the depth is over 15 percent, and it has not recovered by month 8. | | C | none below 70 | 0% | not applicable | No dip: check whether practice really changed | It never falls below 97 percent of the baseline, which can mean the practice did not really change. | **Provenance:** The data and thresholds are illustrative, written for this chapter, and the sim must label them "Illustrative data and rule, not research findings." The idea of the dip is from Fullan. **Rules:** Depth = (baseline − lowest value) ÷ baseline. The lowest point is the month with the smallest value (first such month if tied). Recovery month = the first month at or above the baseline after the lowest point. The judgments follow the rule shown in Content. A normal dip needs all three conditions. Series C is judged "No dip" when its minimum is >= 0.97 × baseline. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the rule and the three series charts. 2. For each series, the learner commits the month of the lowest point and a judgment, and submits them. 3. The sim reveals the depth, the lowest point, and the recovery month, and marks each judgment correct or incorrect with the feedback text. 4. The learner should notice that series C looks the safest and is the one the rule flags for a different reason. **Feedback:** Three series, fixed order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [judgment]. [Why text]." Incorrect: "Not quite. Check the depth, the month of the low point, and the recovery month against the rule. [Why text for the correct answer, without naming the judgment]." The correct judgment is revealed after the attempt. A score "n of 3" is shown. Final message for 3 of 3: "You can tell a normal dip from a warning sign." Otherwise: "Review the rule and try again." **Starting State:** The three charts are shown with the rule, no answers entered, and the prompt "Is each pilot on a normal path?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's worked example (series A) has a baseline of 70, a low of 63 at month 3, a depth of 10 percent, and recovery at month 6, with 78 at month 12. The chapter states that the absence of a dip can itself be a warning. The mastery bar is 3 of 3.
